raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

This ROCm performance change quantizes the BF16 GDN `in_proj_qkvz` and `out_proj` of Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.8 to MXFP4 once after load and runs them on AITER MXFP4 GEMMs instead of BF16 hipBLASLt, because the Quark MXFP4 checkpoints keep both projections in BF16, and cuts median TPOT by **5.1% with NEXTN MTP and 4.0% without MTP** for Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B MXFP4 on 8x MI355X, TP8, geomean over 12 serving shapes on the SGLang main nightly with only this PR added. Output tok/s goes up by 5.9% and 4.2%. The change is opt-in with `SGLANG_ROCM_GDN_ONLINE_MXFP4=in_proj_qkvz,out_proj`.

At TP8, `in_proj_qkvz` is a 4608x8192 weight per GPU and the largest dense weight that every decode and verify step reads. A retuned BF16 GEMM table for these shapes gave no end-to-end gain (99.8% of the current table), and no BF16 kernel we tried beat hipBLASLt on 4608x8192. An MXFP4 weight with its scales is about a quarter of the bytes. At 16 rows, the MXFP4 `in_proj_qkvz` and the BF16 `in_proj_ba` take 8.1 + 7.9 us, and the packed BF16 GEMM of both takes 23.1 us.

## Modifications

- `environ.py` adds `SGLANG_ROCM_GDN_ONLINE_MXFP4`, a comma-separated subset of `in_proj_qkvz,out_proj`. The default is empty.
- `quark_w4a4_mxfp4.py` adds `AiterMxfp4OnlineLinearMethod`. A model sets it on a BF16 linear layer after `create_weights`. The loader then calls `process_weights_after_loading()`, which quantizes the loaded BF16 weight with the existing `dynamic_mxfp4_quant`, preshuffles the weight (16x16) and the E8M0 scales, and records whether AITER has a tuned preshuffled config for (N, K). A second call does nothing. `apply()` quantizes the activation with `per_1x32_f4_quant_hip`. Up to 64 rows with a tuned config, it runs the Triton `gemm_afp4wfp4_preshuffle`. All other batches run the ASM `gemm_a4w4(bpreshuffle=True)`.
- `qwen3_5.py` reads the variable at import. An unknown name raises `ValueError`. Off gfx95x or without `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, it logs a warning and does nothing. Otherwise each GDN layer sets `AiterMxfp4OnlineLinearMethod` on the named projections in `__init__`, so the model loader quantizes them in `load_model`, before SGLang sizes the KV cache and captures the CUDA graphs. It skips projections that the checkpoint already quantized. An MXFP4 `in_proj_qkvz` is no longer an `UnquantizedLinearMethod`, so `finalize_fused_in_proj()` in `prepare_before_cuda_graph_capture` does not build the packed BF16 qkvz+ba GEMM, and `in_proj_ba` (N=32) runs alone in BF16.
- `test/registered/amd/test_qwen35_gdn_online_mxfp4.py` checks both TP8 shapes at 1, 4, 16, 31, 32, 64, 65 and 256 rows against a dequantized FP32 reference. The rows cover both sides of the 32-row scale-layout split and of the 64-row kernel cut. `register_amd_ci` puts it in the MI35x suite, because it skips on anything other than gfx95x.
- `environment_variables.mdx` adds one row for the new variable.

With the variable unset, nothing changes. No layer is quantized, and `finalize_fused_in_proj()` builds the packed BF16 path as before. With it set, only the GDN projections of Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.8 on gfx95x with AITER change.

The Triton path for `in_proj_qkvz` needs the tuned config from [Rocm/aiter5998](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5998) (merged). The AITER pin on main, `2bb549102b` (#44379), includes it. With an older AITER, such as `e7d2453f`, `in_proj_qkvz` takes the ASM path at every row count. The output is still correct there, but we did not measure the speed.

The variable does not support online weight updates, because quantization changes the weight shape and dtype at load. The memory that the BF16 weights free (about 5.5 GB per GPU on Qwen3.8 TP8) goes to the KV cache, because quantization runs before SGLang sizes the pool. The pool grows by 6.4%, from 6.65M to 7.07M tokens with NEXTN and from 7.39M to 7.86M without MTP. The speed tests below ran on the first commit, which quantized after the pool was sized. There, both servers of each pair have the same KV pool, and peak usage was 63% and 56%. The speedup does not come from memory.

## Accuracy Tests

The unit test passes on MI355X, with a relative error below 1e-2 for every shape and row count. It also checks that a second `process_weights_after_loading()` call does not quantize the MXFP4 weight again. It ran in the benchmark job before the servers started.

The end-to-end evals ran on the same servers as "Speed Tests and Profiling" below. BF16 is the same image with the variable unset.

| Eval | NEXTN BF16 | NEXTN MXFP4 | No MTP BF16 | No MTP MXFP4 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GSM8K 5-shot, chat, thinking, flexible-extract (1319) | 0.9765 | 0.9742 | 0.9788 | 0.9818 |
| GPQA Diamond (198, thinking, temperature 1.0) | 0.9343 | 0.9091 | 0.9343 | 0.9242 |
| RULER niah_single_2, 64k | 0.996 | 0.994 | 0.996 | 0.996 |
| RULER niah_single_2, 128k | 0.994 | 0.990 | 0.998 | 0.996 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

8x MI355X, TP8, one node, all four servers in one job. The image is `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.22-rocm10-mi35x-20261016` (SGLang main `34c4ba14c8`, AITER `2bb549102b`) plus the first commit of this PR, `ad94c3c8f2`, and no other change. The later commits change the input check, the CI suite and comments, and move the quantization into the load path. "Load path check" below compares the load path with the first commit. Page size 16, `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1`, fp8 KV cache, `--mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16`, chunked prefill 16384, radix cache off, at most 256 running requests. NEXTN runs use 3 steps, top-k 1, 4 draft tokens, `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec` and `--speculative-draft-model-path` set to the model path. `bench_serve` random dataset, range ratio 0.8, one run per cell.

NEXTN MTP:

| ISL / OSL | Concurrency | TPOT BF16 (ms) | TPOT MXFP4 (ms) | TPOT change | Output tok/s change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8k / 1k | 4 | 6.11 | 6.01 | -1.6% | +3.4% |
| 8k / 1k | 8 | 8.14 | 7.96 | -2.2% | +2.8% |
| 8k / 1k | 16 | 11.70 | 11.28 | -3.6% | +3.6% |
| 8k / 1k | 32 | 18.12 | 17.25 | -4.8% | +5.4% |
| 8k / 1k | 64 | 29.21 | 27.46 | -6.0% | +6.6% |
| 8k / 1k | 128 | 48.70 | 45.86 | -5.8% | +6.6% |
| 8k / 1k | 256 | 92.06 | 85.36 | -7.3% | +8.0% |
| 60k / 600 | 4 | 16.05 | 15.84 | -1.3% | +6.4% |
| 60k / 600 | 16 | 61.08 | 55.69 | -8.8% | +7.0% |
| 60k / 600 | 64 | 245.92 | 228.60 | -7.0% | +7.8% |
| 128k / 1k | 4 | 20.06 | 18.91 | -5.7% | +6.3% |
| 128k / 1k | 16 | 82.98 | 77.75 | -6.3% | +7.1% |
| Geomean | | | | **-5.1%** | **+5.9%** |

No MTP:

| ISL / OSL | Concurrency | TPOT BF16 (ms) | TPOT MXFP4 (ms) | TPOT change | Output tok/s change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8k / 1k | 4 | 13.64 | 13.47 | -1.2% | +1.4% |
| 8k / 1k | 8 | 17.13 | 16.32 | -4.7% | +5.0% |
| 8k / 1k | 16 | 23.36 | 22.44 | -3.9% | +4.1% |
| 8k / 1k | 32 | 32.26 | 31.50 | -2.4% | +2.5% |
| 8k / 1k | 64 | 46.25 | 45.08 | -2.5% | +2.7% |
| 8k / 1k | 128 | 71.55 | 68.90 | -3.7% | +4.0% |
| 8k / 1k | 256 | 119.80 | 113.40 | -5.3% | +5.6% |
| 60k / 600 | 4 | 24.71 | 23.87 | -3.4% | +4.0% |
| 60k / 600 | 16 | 77.35 | 73.17 | -5.4% | +5.8% |
| 60k / 600 | 64 | 268.45 | 252.45 | -6.0% | +6.1% |
| 128k / 1k | 4 | 28.21 | 27.14 | -3.8% | +4.2% |
| 128k / 1k | 16 | 96.83 | 91.48 | -5.5% | +5.5% |
| Geomean | | | | **-4.0%** | **+4.2%** |

Median TTFT is lower in every cell too, by 8.6% (geomean) with NEXTN and 6.5% without MTP. The NEXTN accept length does not drop. `bench_serve` reports a lifetime average per server, and at the end of the run it was 3.14 for BF16 and 3.18 for MXFP4.

The MXFP4 projections run the Triton kernel up to 64 rows and the ASM kernel above that. Prefill always runs ASM. A NEXTN verify step has 4 rows per request, so NEXTN decode runs ASM from concurrency 32 up, and decode without MTP from concurrency 128 up.

Per-call time on one MI355X GPU in the same image, CUDA-graph replays, in us. The MXFP4 times include the activation quant. The BF16 `in_proj` column is what main runs: one packed qkvz+ba GEMM up to 64 rows, and separate qkvz and ba GEMMs above 64 rows. With MXFP4, `in_proj_ba` stays BF16 and runs alone.

| Rows | MXFP4 kernel | BF16 in_proj (qkvz+ba) | MXFP4 qkvz + BF16 ba | BF16 out_proj | MXFP4 out_proj |
| ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | Triton | 16.3 | 10.1 | 6.0 | 4.3 |
| 4 | Triton | 16.7 | 12.8 | 7.0 | 4.9 |
| 16 | Triton | 23.1 | 16.0 | 5.8 | 5.1 |
| 64 | Triton | 22.0 | 20.0 | 7.8 | 6.9 |
| 128 | ASM | 34.8 | 27.8 | 9.9 | 6.6 |
| 256 | ASM | 48.7 | 30.6 | 16.0 | 8.1 |

### Load path check

The same nightly image plus this PR at `0542071e02` (quantization in `prepare_before_cuda_graph_capture`) or at `2c6ceb33c0` (quantization in the load path). Both have `SGLANG_ROCM_GDN_ONLINE_MXFP4=in_proj_qkvz,out_proj` and the flags above. The servers ran on one node in the order capture, load, load, capture, with and without NEXTN. 8k / 1k, one `bench_serve` run per cell and round. The table gives the mean of the two median TPOTs.

| Mode | Concurrency | TPOT at capture (ms) | TPOT in load path (ms) | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| No MTP | 1 | 10.480 | 10.490 | +0.1% |
| No MTP | 4 | 13.455 | 13.460 | +0.0% |
| No MTP | 16 | 22.115 | 22.150 | +0.2% |
| No MTP | 64 | 41.800 | 41.840 | +0.1% |
| NEXTN | 1 | 3.645 | 3.640 | -0.1% |
| NEXTN | 4 | 5.790 | 5.820 | +0.5% |
| NEXTN | 16 | 10.860 | 10.890 | +0.3% |

Between two rounds of the same server, the median TPOT moves by up to 2.8%. Every server logs 138 MXFP4 projections. GSM8K (first 50 questions, 5-shot, chat, thinking, greedy, flexible-extract) gives 0.98 in all four runs without MTP. With NEXTN, it gives 0.98 and 0.96 for each commit. All eight runs miss the same question, and one round of each NEXTN server misses one more, a different question each time.

We ran only Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B MXFP4 at TP8. Qwen3.5 checkpoints and other TP sizes are untested.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| No MTP | 1 | 10.480 | 10.490 | +0.1% |
| No MTP | 4 | 13.455 | 13.460 | +0.0% |
| No MTP | 16 | 22.115 | 22.150 | +0.2% |
| No MTP | 64 | 41.800 | 41.840 | +0.1% |
| NEXTN | 1 | 3.645 | 3.640 | -0.1% |
| NEXTN | 4 | 5.790 | 5.820 | +0.5% |
| NEXTN | 16 | 10.860 | 10.890 | +0.3% |

Between two rounds of the same server, the median TPOT moves by up to 2.8%. Every server logs 138 MXFP4 projections. GSM8K (first 50 questions, 5-shot, chat, thinking, greedy, flexible-extract) gives 0.98 in all four runs without MTP. With NEXTN, it gives 0.98 and 0.96 for each commit. All eight runs miss the same question, and one round of each NEXTN server misses one more, a different question each time.

We ran only Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B MXFP4 at TP8. Qwen3.5 checkpoints and other TP sizes are untested.

+class AiterMxfp4OnlineLinearMethod(LinearMethodBase):
+    """MXFP4 GEMM for a loaded BF16 linear that ``quantize_`` converts once.
+
+    A model sets this method on a BF16 linear after ``create_weights``. The
+    loader then calls ``process_weights_after_loading``, which runs ``quantize_``.
+    ``quantize_`` stores the weight and its E8M0 scales preshuffled. Batches of
+    at most ``PRESHUFFLE_MAX_M`` rows run the Triton preshuffled GEMM if AITER
+    has a tuned config for (N, K). All other batches run the ASM ``gemm_a4w4``.
+    """
+
+    PRESHUFFLE_MAX_M = 64
+
+    @classmethod
+    def quantize_(cls, layer: torch.nn.Module) -> None:
+        from aiter.ops.shuffle import shuffle_scale, shuffle_weight
+        from aiter.ops.triton._triton_kernels.gemm.basic.gemm_afp4wfp4 import (
+            _get_config,
+        )
+
+        w = layer.weight.data
+        n, k = w.shape
+        # gemm_a4w4 and the preshuffled scales read whole 256x256 tiles.
+        assert w.dtype == torch.bfloat16 and n % 256 == 0 and k % 256 == 0, (
+            f"online MXFP4 needs a BF16 weight with N, K % 256 == 0, got {w.dtype} {n}x{k}"
+        )
+        w_q, w_s = _dynamic_mxfp4_quant_orig(w)
+        layer.weight = torch.nn.Parameter(
+            shuffle_weight(w_q.view(torch.uint8), layout=(16, 16)),
+            requires_grad=False,
+        )
+        layer.weight_scale = torch.nn.Parameter(
+            shuffle_scale(w_s.view(torch.uint8)), requires_grad=False
+        )
+        layer.mxfp4_preshuffle_tuned = _get_config(
+            cls.PRESHUFFLE_MAX_M, n, k // 2, True
+        )[1]
+        layer.quant_method = cls()
+
+    def create_weights(self, *args, **kwargs):
+        raise NotImplementedError("use quantize_() on a loaded BF16 linear")
+
+    def process_weights_after_loading(self, layer: torch.nn.Module) -> None:
+        if layer.weight.dtype == torch.bfloat16:
+            self.quantize_(layer)
+
+    def apply(
+        self,
+        layer: torch.nn.Module,
+        x: torch.Tensor,
+        bias: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        from aiter import gemm_a4w4, per_1x32_f4_quant_hip
+        from aiter.ops.triton.gemm_afp4wfp4 import gemm_afp4wfp4_preshuffle
+
+        m, n = x.shape[0], layer.weight.shape[0]
+        w_s = layer.weight_scale
+        if m <= self.PRESHUFFLE_MAX_M and layer.mxfp4_preshuffle_tuned:
+            # Below 32 rows the kernel takes un-shuffled activation scales.
+            x_q, x_s = per_1x32_f4_quant_hip(x, shuffle=m >= 32)
+            x_s = x_s.view(torch.uint8)
+            x_s = x_s.view(x_s.shape[0] // 32, -1) if m >= 32 else x_s[:m]
+            y = torch.empty(m, n, dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device)
+            gemm_afp4wfp4_preshuffle(
+                x_q.view(torch.uint8),
+                layer.weight.view(n // 16, -1),
+                x_s,
+                w_s.view(w_s.shape[0] // 32, -1),
+                x.dtype,
+                y,
+            )
+        else:
+            x_q, x_s = per_1x32_f4_quant_hip(x, shuffle=True)
+            y = gemm_a4w4(
+                x_q,
+                layer.weight.view(x_q.dtype),
+                x_s,
+                w_s.view(x_s.dtype),
+                dtype=x.dtype,
+                bpreshuffle=True,
+            )[:m]
+        return y if bias is None else y + bias

+"""ROCm coverage for the online MXFP4 Qwen3.5/3.8 GDN projections."""
+
+import itertools
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.utils import is_gfx95_supported
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_amd_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_amd_ci(est_time=30, suite="stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x")
+
+# Qwen3.8-2.4T TP8: in_proj_qkvz and out_proj.
+SHAPES = ((4608, 8192), (8192, 2048))
+# Rows on both sides of the 32-row scale-layout split and of the 64-row kernel cut.
+ROWS = (1, 4, 16, 31, 32, 64, 65, 256)
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(
+    torch.cuda.is_available() and torch.version.hip and is_gfx95_supported(),
+    "requires AMD gfx95",
+)
+class TestQwen35GdnOnlineMxfp4(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_matches_dequantized_reference(self):
+        from aiter import per_1x32_f4_quant_hip
+
+        from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.quark.schemes.quark_w4a4_mxfp4 import (
+            AiterMxfp4OnlineLinearMethod,
+            _dequant_mxfp4_to_bf16,
+            _dynamic_mxfp4_quant_orig,
+        )
+
+        for (n, k), m in itertools.product(SHAPES, ROWS):
+            with self.subTest(n=n, k=k, m=m):
+                torch.manual_seed(m)
+                w = torch.randn(n, k, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 0.02
+                x = torch.randn(m, k, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+                w_q, w_s = _dynamic_mxfp4_quant_orig(w)
+                x_q, x_s = per_1x32_f4_quant_hip(x, shuffle=False)
+                ref = torch.nn.functional.linear(
+                    _dequant_mxfp4_to_bf16(
+                        x_q.view(torch.uint8), x_s.view(torch.uint8)[:m]
+                    ).float(),
+                    _dequant_mxfp4_to_bf16(w_q, w_s.contiguous()).float(),
+                )
+
+                layer = torch.nn.Module()
+                layer.weight = torch.nn.Parameter(w, requires_grad=False)
+                layer.quant_method = AiterMxfp4OnlineLinearMethod()
+                # The second call must not quantize the MXFP4 weight again.
+                layer.quant_method.process_weights_after_loading(layer)
+                layer.quant_method.process_weights_after_loading(layer)
+                y = layer.quant_method.apply(layer, x)
+
+                self.assertEqual(y.shape, (m, n))
+                rel = ((y.float() - ref).norm() / ref.norm()).item()
+                self.assertLess(rel, 1e-2)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
